LESSON: LINEAR EQUATIONS

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Algebra 2.1 Algebraic Expressions (5 lessons) • simple algebraic statements • si
Topic 2.2: Linear Equations
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 6

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Linear Equations, part of Algebra 2.1 Algebraic Expressions (5 lessons) • simple algebraic statements • si in Grade 7 MATHEMATICS.

Key inquiry question: How do we use linear equations in real-life? 2. Why do we use linear equations in real-life?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. role play activities involving equations with one unknown for example weighing using beam balance. Also, dramatise shopping activities.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. role play activities involving equations with one unknown for example weighing using beam balance. Also, dramatise shopping activities.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Linear Equations together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and Collaboration: speaking, listening and teamwork as the learner role plays activities involving equations

in one unknown.

● Self-efficacy: self-awareness skills as the learner carries out weighing using beam balance and role play different activities.

● Learning to learn: organising own learning as the learner applies linear equations in real-life.

Values

● Integrity as the learner shares resources as per the given equation (conditions).

● Responsibility: as the learner uses a given letter in the equation to represent an item.
